analysis: Integration of the waitlist PR: a CLI-only feature adds a new use of the A-008 login bearer token. The client does GET /v1/waitlists, GET /v1/waitlists/{feature} and POST /v1/waitlists/{feature}. It sends a fixed body {} and nothing about the Mac. Documented and unit-tested controls: https-only or loopback http, no redirects, 10 s timeout, 64 KiB cap, no cookies, and coordinator-supplied text stripped of control, format and bidi characters (printable()) plus --json escaping. These appear to block terminal escape injection and token leakage via redirect. I did not see the production source for FeatureWaitlist.swift, FeatureWaitlistGate.swift or WaitlistCommand.swift, and I confirmed the controls only through doc text, tests and the earlier source analyses. The gates are wired in ClusterSetupWizardCommand.runOnboarding (head ~116, 135-153) and SandboxSetupCommand (.fresh path only, before checkMac and the installer download). They are product-access gates, not security boundaries. The 404 fail-open, the paired-Mac exemption and the unreadable-pairing exemption all rely on a user-controlled local client, and the coordinator or sandbox service must enforce access. TB-013/T-061 installer controls (https, 1 MiB cap, shebang, 0700/0600 staging, no --force) are unchanged. The gate only adds a pre-check. Tests inject waitlist: .approved, which is test-only and adds no production attack surface. The T-041 cache, TB-011 and TB-014 are not touched. Open questions for later review: (1) whether the token sent by WaitlistCommand (AuthTokenStore.load at WaitlistCommand.swift:36) respects the A-008 issuer binding when the config or --config points to a different coordinator; (2) the loopback allowlist handling of IPv6 "[::1]" (fails closed at worst); (3) that production SandboxSetupFlow defaults waitlist to the live check and not .approved; (4) the sandbox, cluster service and link-follower routes that bypass runOnboarding; (5) head docs ranges 1360-1385 and 1635-1724. No finding is supported by the supplied evidence.
